name: Baobabs and the ginkgo — ancient landmark trees
status: 4 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: All 8 baobab species (Africa, Madagascar, Australia) and the ginkgo. Both are 'landmark' trees: individually rare, huge or ancient, worth a place name; the events/lore system may name them. Baobabs are bat-pollinated night-bloomers and shed leaves in the dry season; hollow old ones shelter camps and bees. Ginkgo turns gold and drops every leaf in a week.

canopy.name: African baobab
canopy.source: African savanna, Sahel to Limpopo. The upside-down tree; thousands of years old; hollow trunks shelter people and bees. All 8 Kew-accepted species. Deciduous in the dry season, bat-pollinated white flowers at night, fruit by mammals.

traits.leaf_shape: compound or lobed leaves in a flat spreading crown
traits.trunk: single trunk, flat-topped crown or, for herbs, a huge single leaf on a stalk
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

canopy.name: Ginkgo
canopy.source: Wild in the Tianmu and Dalou mountains of E China; the last of its line, unchanged since the dinosaurs. Fan leaves turn pure gold in one week each autumn, then drop all at once. Dioecious; wind-pollinated; fetid seeds carried by mammals. Kew POWO.

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
